## Reusable lesson

The brief's instinct to distrust a region table's *interpretation* was right
twice, in both directions. `.coords` and the brass corners were both reported
as "lacquer gradient error"; both were something else entirely — one a
centring constant, one a gradient that was simply unreachable *by the route
the notes had assumed*. And the title's phantom regression was a corner drawn
in the wrong place. **Blockmaps localise; they do not explain.**

# Round 5 — the piece gradient bake, and a confirmed defect that was not one

Baseline re-measured first and reproduced exactly: **214 943 @ tol 8 (20.58%),
mean |Δ| 7.09, 34 621 @ tol 24**, 1280x816, `wait:8`.

| # | change | tol 8 | tol 24 | mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | baseline (round 4 close) | 214 943 | 34 621 | 7.09 |
| 1 | `B` verb's missing 7th argument (`1.00`) | 214 943 | 34 621 | 7.09 |
| 2 | piece gIv/gEb gradient baked (6 types × 2 colours) | **200 664** | **30 812** | **6.77** |

Net for the round: **−14 279 @ tol 8, −3 809 @ tol 24, mean −0.32**.
The entire win is inside `board_interior 80,72-752,744`; all eleven regions
were re-measured and **every other one is byte-identical to its round-4 value**,
so nothing regressed.

## 1. The `B` verb — a real defect, and the stated consequence was false

`app.nim:710` emits six arguments; `skia_shim.cpp:1343-1344` reads seven
(`x y w h radius COLOR width`), so `CmdReader::num()` (`:1188-1195`) hit the
trailing `;`, `strtof` failed, and it returned 0. That much is real, and the
code comment claiming otherwise was wrong.

**But the brief's two claims about the consequence are both wrong**, and it
matters because they are the kind of claim that costs a round:

* It is **not** the piece rim. `app.nim:710` is inside `drawFrame` — it is the
  **frame's** border, `inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,.6)` from html:58. The piece
  rim is drawn through a different verb entirely: `d.svgPath(path, x0, y0, sc,
  strC, 1.5)` at `app.nim:1065`, which is the `S` verb, and `S` *does* pass its
  width.
* A zero stroke width does **not** draw nothing. Skia renders
  `kStroke_Style` at width 0 as a 1px **hairline**. Measured before the fix, at
  col x=36 the port read (25.9,9.3,5.7) against a lacquer of (65.7,24.0,14.8)
  — a ratio of 0.394, which is exactly `1 - 0.6`, the `rgba(0,0,0,.6)` inset.
  The rim was already there, at the right strength, in the right place.

The fix (append `1.00`, read from html:58's `1px` — not guessed) is correct
regardless and is banked, but it buys **exactly 0 pixels** at both
tolerances: the frame is byte-identical. On this geometry Skia's hairline and
a 1.0 stroke are the same pixels. See `apps/chess/.board/c2/`.

## 2. The piece gradient — the bake DOES reach what a Draw verb cannot

This was the one item on the list marked "blocked", with the hint to apply the
brass-corner trick. It works, and it is the largest single win available on
this page. The port now rasterises the pieces itself:

* a small SVG path parser (M/L/H/V/C/A/Z, abs + rel) with beziers flattened
  at 20 steps and arcs at 1 step per 2°, in `flattenPath`;
* antialiased **nonzero winding** — 4 scanlines per pixel row with exact
  horizontal span coverage, in `fillCov`;
* a stroke band from a distance-to-polyline that is only evaluated near the
  boundary (`markNear` marks candidates from the scanline crossings; a full
  w×h×|p| field would have been 64M ops across all 31 paths);
* the gradient sampled per pixel.

`path ∩ gradient` is still unreachable (defect 6 stands: `runCmds` has no
gradient verb and its only clip is `clipRect`), but **the engine never has to
do the intersection** — that is the whole trick, and it is why the corner bake
generalises.

### The gradient is PER-PATH, not per-piece

`gradientUnits` defaults to `objectBoundingBox`, which is the bbox of the
element that **references** the gradient — each `<path>`, not the enclosing
`<svg>`. This is worth stating because the union is the intuitive guess and it
is wrong by 22 units. Measured on the a1 rook at y=690, which crosses the
crenellation path (bbox x31–69, y23–40.5):

| model | predicted at x=134 | reference |
|---|---|---|
| per-path bbox | (190.8,164.4,124.8) | **(189,162,122)** |
| union of all five rook paths | (211.5,191.0,155.7) | (189,162,122) |

Result: the piece body now matches the reference to **d = 0–1 across the whole
body** (x=110→136 read 248,242,228 → 189,162,122 in both), and the black
pieces match to d ≤ 1. The silhouettes did not move.

### Paint order changed as a side effect

The old code replayed each path as *stroke then fill* because `F`+`S` on one
path is broken (reference/16 §1); that loses the stroke's inner half, so the
outline was 0.63px instead of 1.26px. The bake composites fill-then-stroke,
which is SVG's actual order and what Chrome rendered, so the full outline is
now visible. This is confounded with the gradient change in the same build —
the measured −3 809 is the net of both, not the gradient alone.

### Two bugs worth writing down

Both were found by a **native** harness, `.board/c2/raster_test.nim`, which
compiles the same procs with `nim js` and prints bboxes and per-row ink. The
wasm render hung for **5+ minutes** on the first attempt; the harness made it a
one-line read. Native `nim c` is not available here (msys gcc cannot execute
`cc1`) — `nim js -d:nodejs` is the workaround, and it is fast enough to
iterate in seconds.

1. **The M-pair re-read.** A command must consume numbers only when a number
   actually *follows* it. The obvious formulation — always run `case cmd` —
   re-reads `M24 91c…`'s `91` as an implicit lineto, because M leaves
   `cmd = 'L'` behind, silently corrupting `cx` on every path shaped
   `M<a> <b><letter>`.
2. **`xs` was never cleared between scanlines.** `crossings` appends to a
   `seq` that lived across the whole loop, so every scanline inherited the
   previous one's crossings. The symptom was deceptive: the top of a shape was
   correct and it then bled to the bottom of the tile — the rook base filled
   device rows 69–91 instead of 69–76. **A rasteriser that fills too much looks
   exactly like a rasteriser with a geometry bug.** The per-row ink table from
   the harness, not the overall image, is what caught it.

## What this re-ranks

With the board interior down to **11 725 @ tol 24**, the remaining structure
budget is:

| region | tol 24 | reachable? |
|---|---|---|
| board_interior | 11 725 | partly — see below |
| title | 5 575 | defect 1, glyphs |
| scoresheet | 5 383 | defect 1, glyphs |
| frame_above / below / left / right | 1 648 / 1 169 / 882 / 787 | mixed |
| buttons / status / tray / hint | 1 215 / 1 205 / 1 202 / 1 073 | glyphs + defect 5 |

The pieces are no longer "blocked": what is left inside the board is ~6 500 px
of silhouette-scale error (deltas 45–200, the dark ebony pieces against light
board) and ~4 400 px of tone (25–45). **The gradient axis is now nearly
exhausted; what remains on the pieces is geometry, not colour**, and that is a
much harder problem than a ramp.

## Engine defect confirmed (not new, but now precisely stated)

**Defect 6 is real and load-bearing.** There is no way to express
`path ∩ gradient` through `Draw`: `runCmds` verbs are M L H V C A Z F S R B E
G T I P p b Y X V K t s o O, plus `svgPath` via the SDK — no gradient, and the
only clip is `clipRect`. `Canvas.fillGradient` (`nimskia.nim:133`) exists but is
**rrect-only** and is not reachable from an app module. Only a bake gets there.

Also re-confirmed, cheaply: **a `.wasm` byte count is not a build fingerprint.**
Three builds of this app differed by 4 bytes (325 822 → 325 826 → 373 889) for
three genuinely different programs, and the render is what identified them.

## 3. `inset 0 -2px 6px` — worth zero pixels, and it took the page down

Two things happened here, and the second is worth more than the first.

### The latent `erfA` stack overflow (the real find)

Modelling the bottom inset properly means clamping distance-to-edge at 0. The
first build with that clamp **rendered nothing at all**:

```
crashed=[trap in yantra_main: error while executing at wasm backtrace:
    0:  0x348c0 - ch.wasm!erfA__app_u197
    1:  0x3497f - ch.wasm!erfA__app_u197
   ... 19 identical frames ...
Caused by: memory fault at wasm address 0x10000000c
           wasm trap: out of bounds memory access
] now=800.0
```

`erfA` exploited oddness with `if x <= 0.0: return -erfA(-x)`. IEEE says
`-0.0 <= 0.0` is **true**, so `erfA(0.0)` recurses on itself until the stack
dies. Rounds 1-4 never hit it because no caller ever passed exactly 0 — it is
a **latent trap that any caller passing 0 will find**, and it presents as an
unattributable whole-app memory fault, not as an error in the thing you
changed. Fixed with `if x < 0.0`: `x = 0` needs no special case at all, because
`ERF_TAB[0]` **is** `erf(0) = 0` and the table branch already answers it. The
comment now says so.

This is the third time on this page that a plausible one-token change has been
the whole difference, and it is the reason the crash was worth more than the
shadow: it was not reachable by reading, only by doing.

### The shadow itself: a measured zero

| | tol 8 | tol 24 | mean | band worst |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| linear 6px ramp, half-size bake | 200 664 | 30 812 | 6.77 | dR 7 |
| fitted Gaussian (σ 3.69, edge ly 757.33) | **200 659** | **30 812** | **6.76** | **dR 2** |

**−5 pixels at tol 8, zero at tol 24.** Predicted before the build, from the
histogram: the band's worst |Δ| was 7, under the tol-8 threshold, and the
1 648 px that `frame_below` still carries at tol 24 are coord-label glyph
edges, not this shadow. The fit is right (d≤2 across the whole band, from d≤7),
but a correct fix that cannot move a threshold is a correct fix and nothing
else.

Two things were wrong, not one. The old model was a *linear* ramp where Chrome
draws a Gaussian; and because the bake is half size (`ly` steps by `B/FRW =
2.0`), the guard `ly > B-2` fired on **one bake row out of 380** — so the
shadow was effectively *absent*, not merely misshapen. Measured alpha at the
bottom edge (col 400; col 120 agrees to 1, so it is uniform in x):

    row  778 780 781 782 783 784 785 786
    a     .024 .024 .048 .071 .119 .167 .214 .286

Fitting `0.5 * cGauss(g, sigma)` gives the shadow edge at ly = 757.33 with
**σ = 3.69** — about **1.23×** the CSS nominal 3. That is the same direction and
roughly the same magnitude as every other blur this port has needed, and it is
now the fourth independent measurement of the same effect. It is a property of
this port's baking, not of this page.

## Round 6

Baseline carried in: **200 659** @tol8 (19.21%), **30 812** @tol24 (2.95%), mean 6.76.
Chess reference noise floor, re-measured this round against
`.board/probe/refr2_chess.png`: **18 029 px (1.73%) @tol8**, **14 761 px (1.41%)
@tol24**. Quote every figure against that spread.

### 6.1 Board tone: the squares are individually randomised, not one fixed wash

`bakeBoard()` applied a single fixed 90° wash at fixed α 0.05/0.06 to all 64
squares. `070-chess-study.html:537-549` instead runs an LCG per square
(`seed = 90210`, Park–Miller `seed*16807 % 2147483647`) and derives **three** CSS
custom properties per square: `--ga` (gradient angle, light squares
`88 + rnd*6`, dark `-3 + rnd*6`), `--v1` (`0.02 + rnd*0.07`), `--v2`
(`0.02 + rnd*0.08`). The port now replays that LCG and stores angle + both alphas
per square. Note the ordering: `light` is decided from the **raw** index `s`
*before* the flip at html:557, so the light/dark test is
`((s shr 3) + (s and 7)) and 1 == 1` on the un-flipped index.

`int64` is mandatory here — `seed*16807` reaches 3.6e13 and silently overflows
int32.

Diagnostic proof the fix was correct, and the reason to trust it beyond the
score: the ranks with **no pieces on them** went to ~zero structural error
(rank5 314 → 2, rank6 79 → 30, rank4 202 → 26 @tol24). Error there could only
have been board tone, and only board tone changed.

    board interior @tol24   11 452   ->  11 035
    whole frame  @tol8    200 659   ->  179 631   (-21 028)
    whole frame  @tol24    30 812   ->   30 122   (   -690)
    mean                    6.76     ->    6.48

The tol-8 move is ~12× the 1.73% floor. **The tol-24 move of -690 is inside the
1.41% floor band** and must not be claimed as significant on its own; the
tol-8 figure is the honest headline for this change.

### 6.2 Item 3, piece geometry — `flattenPath`'s arc branch was wrong

This is the "drawn from the wrong source geometry" item. It was **not** the path
data: all six symbols in `app.nim:386-451` are verbatim against
`070-chess-study.html:235-299`, re-checked character by character. The defect is
in the rasteriser that consumes them.

`app.nim:1215-1226` computed the SVG arc's start and sweep angles with
`arccos` plus a cross-product sign, and derived the *endpoint* direction from
`(ox - rx*cs - cx, oy - rx*sn - cy)` — a vector that is not the endpoint at all.
For a semicircle both are wrong. Replaying both formulations
(`apps/chess/.board/ch6/arcdbg2.mjs`) on the five round shapes in the pieces:

| shape | old endpoint error | new |
|---|---|---|
| pawn head `M50 32.5a13.5…` | 24.9447 units | 0.0000 |
| bishop ball | 8.3149 | 0.0000 |
| queen ball (x30) | 5.3585 | 0.0000 |
| queen ball (x57) | 5.3585 | 0.0000 |
| queen finial | 8.4997 | 0.0000 |

24.94 units is nearly **twice the 13.5-unit pawn head radius**: the flattened arc
never reached its own endpoint, so the fill closed on a wedge and every round
shape in every piece had a bite taken out of it, with the blurred drop-shadow
layer showing through. The old code produced th0 = 90° where -90° was correct
and dth = 225° where 180° was correct.

Confirmed on the frame before the fix — e2, row 620, the port painted the pawn
head as a flat `121,104,81` where the reference carries a continuous bright
ivory fill ramping `232,219,193 → 193,168,129`: a ~105-level dark hole straight
through the middle of the piece.

The fix replaces the angle helper with `atan2` on the start and end radii in the
ellipse's own frame:

```nim
let u1x = (cx-ox)*cs + (cy-oy)*sn
let u1y = -(cx-ox)*sn + (cy-oy)*cs
let u2x = (x-ox)*cs  + (y-oy)*sn
let u2y = -(x-ox)*sn  + (y-oy)*cs
let th0 = arctan2(u1y, u1x)
var dth = arctan2(u2y, u2x) - th0
```

Nim spells it `arctan2`, not `atan2`.

    board interior @tol24   11 035   ->   9 130   (-1 905)
    whole frame  @tol8    179 631   ->  177 501   (-2 130)
    whole frame  @tol24    30 122   ->   28 217   (-1 905)
    mean                    6.48     ->    6.32

Ranks 1-2 (white) 6 687 → 5 497; rank 7 2 439 → 1 730; ranks 3-6 unchanged, as
expected for empty ranks.

### 6.3 Reported, not fixed: an unexplained dark lens on d3

The reference carries a dark lens of ~138 reference-only pixels at the top of
d3 (rect x332-416 y492-576, rows 497-507) that the port does not have at all.

* **It is real, not noise.** It reproduces independently in the second chess
  capture `.board/probe/refr2_chess.png` — 748 ink px in that rect there, 0 in
  the port (`apps/chess/.board/ch6/glyph.mjs`).
* **It is not `.sq.ring::after`.** Fitting a circle to the reference-only ink
  (`apps/chess/.board/ch6/ring.mjs`) gives radii spread over 13.2 .. 58.7 with
  median 47.7, whereas that gradient's band on an 84px square is
  r = 36.8 .. 44.0. No match.
* Only d3 is affected; the same rows on a-, b-, c-, e-, f- and g-file are clean.

At 199 px @tol24 it is small. Flagging rather than guessing: **I cannot attribute
it to a named CSS construct.**

### 6.4 Ruled lines in the score sheet — checked, no change needed

The 26px repeating rule (`rgba(70,110,150,.18)`, html:162) was suspected of a
2px phase error. Measured with `apps/chess/.board/ch6/lines.mjs`: reference dark
rows at 387, 413, 439; port at 387, 413, 439. **Pitch and phase agree exactly** —
no change made. The residual at that band is glyph error.

The **intermittent `out of bounds memory access`** in #70. Not reproduced this

bounds from division. Note that 6.2 *removed* an unbounded-arc code path (the
old one produced a 225° sweep where 180° was correct), which is adjacent to that
class — but that is not proof it was the same bug and it is not claimed as such.

**The single most valuable thing this lane produced is not a pixel count.** It is

# Round 7 — the reference, not the port

**Starting point**: the baselines quoted in the brief, re-measured here:
shipped ref070.png vs the unchanged port: **58.54% / 45.51% @tol24 / mean 52.68**.
Much worse than the round-6 close (17.20% / 3.70% @tol24 / mean 6.32),
but the port is unchanged — the reference moved, not the code.

## The reference is still a 1296-wide layout cropped to 1280×816

`capture-ref.ps1`'s R18 probe reports `clientWidth/clientHeight = 1280×816`,
but Chrome's `100vw`/`100vh` resolve to the **window size** (1296×911).
The script crops the 1296-wide screenshot to 1280×816, producing a PNG that
looks right (correct left-edge desk border) but whose layout is a 1296-wide
one shifted left and cut at the right.

Independent captures at each window size, decoded with two independent
PNG decoders (both agree; crop.mjs's re-encode was not the cause):

| window | board pitch | board x | panel x | port matches? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1296×911** (shipped ref) | **88** | **74** | **863** | no — 58.54% |
| 1280×816 (true viewport) | **84** | **80** | **834** | **18.11%** |
| 1264×721 (old broken) | **~73.5** | ~114 | ~778 | — |

The port's constants (`FX=36, FY=28, B=760, FR≈44, PX=834.2`) are
**verified correct** against the 1280×816 layout: `--B = min(100vh-56,
100vw-500) = 760`, `--fr = B*.058 ≈ 44`, board 672, pitch 84, panel
x = 36+760+gap ≈ 834.

## Numbers for the report

| comparison | tol 8 | tol 24 | mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| port vs shipped ref070 | 58.54% | 45.51% | 52.68 |
| port vs true 1280×816 capture | **18.11%** | 3.86% | 7.43 |
| shipped ref070 vs true 1280×816 | 57.14% | 45.08% | 51.73 |

| round-6 floor | 1.73% | 1.41% | — |

## Attribution

- **No viewport compensation in app.nim.** `SW=1280`, `SH=816`, no
  `clientWidth/clientHeight` reads, no 1264/719 literals. The earlier
  typewriter bug (SW=1264/SH=719.5 back-solving a broken reference) is
  **not present here**.
- **Attributable to tooling**: R18a is not fixed — the probe verifies
  `innerWidth/clientWidth`, the page renders at the window width, and
  the crop preserves the wrong layout. The same defect that created
  the 1264×721 references (R18) recurs in a subtler form.

## RESOLVED at round 139 — this analysis was right, the fix was elsewhere

R7 diagnosed the *symptom* correctly (ref070 carried a 1296-wide layout) and
blamed "capture-ref.ps1's probe-to-window mapping". That is right about the
mechanism and wrong about the fix, in a way that cost two more rounds:

R18/R18b did not *fail* to compensate — it compensated unconditionally. The
right compensation depends on which CSS metric the page lays out against, and
`100vw` and `clientWidth` resolve to different numbers at the same window size
(innerWidth=1264 vs 100vw=1280 at `--window-size=1280,816`). Forcing a
scrollbar onto the probe made the overhead 16 px larger and therefore correct
only for `clientWidth` pages. Chess lays out off `100vw`, so for chess the
compensated capture was the *wrong* one — 18.42% at no-overhead vs 58.57% at
overhead, measured both ways.

So R7's item 1 ("orchestrator must fix the probe-to-window mapping") is
answered, but not by fixing the mapping. The fix is `capture-ref.ps1`'s new
6th argument `nooverhead`, and chess is a `nooverhead` page. Full entry in
`.board/reports/ISSUES.md` as R18c.

R7's item 2 is done. Re-measured against a correctly-captured 1280×816
reference: **18.42% @tol8, mean 8.02** (was reported 18.11% against a
hand-made capture — 0.31pp apart, which is the grain floor of the reference,
not a change in the port). The port's own layout constants
(`FX=36, FY=28, B=760, FR≈44, PX=834.2`) are confirmed correct against it.

R7's item 3 stands: typeface/glyph error and the intermittent crash are the
port's own remaining work, and they are now measured against a reference that
can actually refute them.

## Next item

1. 18.42% @tol8 / 3.86% @tol24 vs a correct reference is the honest baseline.
   The structural residual is ~44k px; the rest is feTurbulence grain.
2. Port's own reachable residual: typeface/glyph error (defect 1) and
   the intermittent crash (defect class noted R6).

### 17.24 Defect 7 done — and the 11 000 px prediction was wrong by an order of magnitude

Item 7 said `Draw.text` cannot name a typeface, cost this page ~11 000 px, and had been
corrected in round 156 from "cannot" to "not yet done here". So: done.

**All 9 `d.text` call sites moved to `Draw.textFace` with `"Palatino Linotype"`.**

Choosing the family was not a guess. The page's stack is `--serif: Baskerville, Baskerville
Old Face, Hoefler Text, Garamond, Palatino Linotype, Book Antiqua, P052, URW Palladio L,
Georgia, serif` (`070-chess-study.html:22`). Checked against `%WINDIR%\Fonts`: Baskerville,
Garamond and P052 are all **absent**; Palatino Linotype (`pala.ttf`), Georgia, Times,
Cambria and Constantia are present. So the capture browser resolved to **Palatino Linotype**
too, and the port now matches what the reference actually drew. `Draw.text` emits the `T`
verb, which the shim renders in the engine default — Segoe UI — so before this the entire
page was set in a sans face against a serif reference.

**Measured against `.board/frames/ref070.png` at tol 8, both frames rendered at `wait:8`:**

| | differing px | mean abs delta |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (`Draw.text`, Segoe UI) | 177 501 / 1 044 480 (**16.99 %**) | 6.32 |
| **`textFace`, Palatino Linotype** | 176 455 / 1 044 480 (**16.89 %**) | **6.09** |

Both metrics moved the right way, so the change is real. But it is **1 046 px, not the
11 000 the note predicted** — an order of magnitude short, and the prediction is the thing
that needs correcting. It was an estimate of tracking drift multiplied out by an area guess,
never measured, and it was wrong.

**The more informative number is that the change moved 12 376 pixels of the frame.** So the
old font was wrong over a large area and the new one is wrong over nearly as much of it;
only ~8 % of the churn was a net correction. Wrong pixels are not the same as pixels the
right font fixes, and I conflated the two when writing the estimate.

**Where the text still disagrees**, from differencing the two rendered frames rather than
against the reference (bands of rows that moved at all):

    y   32.. 90   (h1 "Grandmaster's Study")        y  408.. 423   1443 px
    y  107.. 120    153 px                            y  442.. 456   1253 px
    y  149.. 163    698 px                            y  527.. 540    123 px
    y  191.. 204     89 px                            y  611.. 624    129 px
    y  229.. 240    405 px                            y  695.. 708     97 px
    y  275.. 295                                      y  759.. 776   1469 px
    y  321.. 328    266 px
    y  380.. 389    464 px

**The next step is the `spaced` proc, and the change made it worse rather than better.**
`spaced` (`app.nim:276`) advances by `size * 0.667 + track` — a single constant chosen for
Segoe UI's metrics, applied per character. Palatino Linotype has different advances, so
every letter-spaced run (the `WHITE`/`BLACK` labels at y 107-120 and y 149-163, and the
piece captions) now drifts at a new rate. **That constant is per-family and was never
measured**; defect 1 (no text measure API) is what makes it a constant at all. Re-tuning it
against Palatino is the next measurable move, and it should be done by measuring rendered
run extents rather than by fitting a number to the reference.

### 17.25 Defect 1 finally has a number, and a control

17.24 left the `spaced` proc: it advances by `size * 0.667 + track`, one constant per
character, picked for Segoe. Changing the family does not change the advance, so the swap
fixed the glyph shapes and left the spacing exactly as wrong as before.

**Two tools were needed first, both in `tools/`:**

- `png2raw.mjs` — decode a PNG reference to raw RGBA. Every existing probe reads `.raw`,
  and the only way to compare against the reference was `pngdiff.mjs`, which reports a
  whole-frame score and cannot answer "which pixels hold this text". **Validated by
  decoding `ref070.png` and differencing it against itself: 0 / 1 044 480 at tol 0, mean
  0.00.** A measuring tool that has not been checked against its own input is not a tool.
- `textextent.mjs` — per-column ink profile of a band, reported as glyph clusters and
  inter-glyph advances. Takes an optional colour key (`minRB`, minimum red-minus-blue).

The colour key is what made this possible. The runs **overlap vertically** — the eyebrow is
drawn at y=28 size 12 and the h1 at y=45 size 34.56, so both put ink in rows 19-38 and no y
band separates them. By colour they separate cleanly: `C_BRASS 0xC9A45C` has R-B = **109**,
`C_IVORY 0xF7F0E1` has R-B = **22**. Keying at R-B >= 60 isolates the eyebrow in both frames.

**Measured — two independent runs, with the Segoe build as a control:**

| run | size | track | reference | port, Palatino | port, Segoe | excess/char |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `A HOT-SEAT GAME FOR TWO` (23 ch) | 12 | 4.08 | **261 px** | 275 px | 275 px | **0.61** |
| `SCORE SHEET` (11 ch) | 13 | 3.9 | **127 px** | 134 px | 132 px | **0.64** |

**The control is the finding.** Palatino and Segoe produce the *same* 275 px eyebrow span,
because the advance is a constant that never sees the family. So none of the drift is
typographic — all of it is the `0.667`. That is the first statement about this defect that is
attributable, and it retires the plausible reading that the font swap should have improved
spacing.

Solving `size * (0.667 - k)` from the two runs independently gives **k = 0.616** and
**k = 0.618**. Consistent to 0.002 across different sizes, tracks and strings — so the drift
is systematic, not a per-string coincidence.

Glyph clusters tell the same story from the other side: the reference resolves **19** and
**10** separate glyphs, the port **17** and **9**. Characters are colliding into blobs.

**And I am still not changing the constant.** 0.617 is the mean advance of the *particular
strings on this page*, not a property of Palatino Linotype — a run of `I` would be far
narrower and a run of `W` far wider, and no single number can be right for both. Changing
0.667 to 0.617 would move the scoreboard without fixing the cause, which is the same trade
as fitting `rx ≈ 376` and is refused for the same reason. **The cause is defect 1: the app
cannot measure text.** The fix is a measure query in the SDK — the shim already has
`yk_text_draw2` and Skia has `measureText`; what is missing is a way for a `Draw` producer to
*ask* for advances before it commits to pen positions.

**What changed is that the gap is now quantified rather than gestural.** §17.24's standing
note said "the next measurable move". It was measurable, it took two tools and a control,
and the answer is **~0.6 px per character, entirely attributable to one constant, and not
fixable from app code.** That is the first time this defect has had a number attached to it.

### 17.27 Letter-spacing ELIMINATED as a cause, and the 0.667 "calibration" corrected

Round 163 showed dna's `MONO_ADV = 0.5498047 ## Consolas hmtx advance / unitsPerEm` — a
hand-built advance table that encodes one font's metrics. Chess's `spaced()` advances by a
single flat `size * 0.667 + track` for **every** glyph, which is the same kind of stand-in.
So the question this round settled is: does the flat constant explain the 16.89 %?

**Deriving per-glyph advances from the reference.** A font advance is a property of the
typeface, and the reference renders that typeface, so the reference's own glyph origins ARE
the advance values. For each glyph in "A HOT-SEAT GAME FOR TWO":

    advance(c) = (origin_to_origin_spacing − track) / size,  track = 12 × 0.34 = 4.080px

Advances that **skip a space** (A→H, T→G, E→F, R→T) also carry the space's width and are
discarded — reading one as a single glyph produced a *negative* advance for `A`, which is how
the bug was caught.

**The table (em), and the check that it is real:**

| ch | em | ch | em | ch | em |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `-` | 0.3267 | `S` | 0.4933 | `O` | 0.7433 |
| `E`,`F` | 0.5767 | `T` | 0.6600 | `H` | 0.8267 |
| `G` | 0.7433 | `A` | 0.7850 | `M`,`W` | 0.9933 |

**`O` occurs twice and measures 0.743 both times; `T` occurs twice and measures 0.660 both
times.** That exact repeat agreement is the evidence this is measurement and not noise —
a fitted coefficient would not reproduce the same character to the same 1/1000 em twice.
`A` differs (0.743 / 0.827) by exactly the ±1 px quantisation, since cluster origins are
integer pixel columns. **Range 0.327 → 0.993 em, a 0.667 em spread.** The hyphen is 51 %
narrower than the flat constant gave it; `M` and `W` are 49 % wider.

**So the constant is wrong — and fixing it changes nothing.**

| build | differing px | % | mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| HEAD, flat 0.667 | 176 454 | 16.89 % | 6.09 |
| per-glyph table | 176 416 | 16.89 % | 6.08 |

Net **39 pixels out of 1 044 480**. Worse in 19 rows, better in 28, unchanged in 769. **That is
noise, so the table was reverted** and `0.667` stays — shipping 30 lines of "measured" values
for a 0.004 % move that is not even directionally uniform would make the code look more
precise than it is. Rule: *different is not better; prove it moves toward the reference.*

**The result worth keeping is the elimination.** A hypothesis is properly killed by a correct
implementation of it, not by an argument. The advance really does span 0.67 em, the constant
really was wrong, and implementing the right answer moved the scoreboard by 39 pixels.
**Letter-spacing is not what keeps this page at 16.89 %.** That is now settled and should not
be re-litigated.

**And the header's claim was simply false.** `app.nim` said 0.667 was "calibrated against the
reference eyebrow … measures 278px wide = 12.1px per character". Measured: the reference
eyebrow's ink spans **x 835..1094 = 260 px** across 19 glyphs; this port's own render spans
**273 px**. 278 is neither. **0.667 reproduces the PORT, not the reference** — and my
port-notes had recorded that I declined to fit this coefficient, while the code carried a
fitted one and described it as calibrated. The comment is corrected in place; the code is
unchanged, and the corrected build scores 176 454 — byte-identical to HEAD, which is what a
comment-only change must do.

Where the remaining error lives is therefore **not** spacing: defect 1 (+1.68/255 per
translucent fill, measured) and the 0.61 px/char text metric still stand, and nothing here
contradicts them.

TITLE: Helix — The Double Helix Explained
FILE: 052-dna-helix.html

=== PROMPT (exact prompt used) ===
Build "Helix — The Double Helix Explained", an educational, beautiful interactive visualization. Centre: a rotating B-DNA double helix drawn on canvas with 3D projection — two sugar-phosphate backbones as glossy ribbons (#2ec4b6 and #e71d36 with depth shading) and base pairs as rungs coloured by nucleotide (A #ff9f1c, T #ffbf69, G #6a4c93, C #8ac926), with correct pairing (A–T, G–C), ~10.5 base pairs per turn, and depth fading for the back strands. A clean biotech palette on off-white (#f7f9fb) with a dark-mode toggle. A side panel with annotations and leader lines (major/minor groove; hydrogen bonds: 2 for A–T, 3 for G–C; 5'→3' direction), a sequence input where typing A/T/G/C rebuilds the helix live (auto-generating the complementary strand), and an "Unzip" button that animates replication — the strands separate and new complementary nucleotides float in. Interaction: drag to rotate, scroll to zoom, hover a base pair to highlight and label it. Typography: a modern sans with a monospace sequence display.

SHARED REQUIREMENTS (apply to every page in this 100-page collection):
1. One standalone HTML5 file. All CSS inline in <style>, all JavaScript inline in <script>. No external resources of any kind: no CDN, no libraries, no web fonts, no external images/SVG/audio files, no network requests. All visuals come from CSS, inline SVG, Canvas and procedural code.
2. Valid HTML5: <!DOCTYPE html>, <html lang="en">, <meta charset="utf-8">, a viewport meta tag, a meaningful <title> and meta description, well-nested semantic markup, unique ids, labels/aria attributes for controls, <button type="button"> for actions.
3. Typography from local system font stacks only, always ending in a generic family; display lettering may be drawn with SVG or Canvas.
4. Responsive from 360px phones to large desktops with no horizontal page scroll; canvases match their container and devicePixelRatio (capped at 2) and re-layout on resize.
5. Works offline by opening the file directly (file://); no console errors; storage access guarded with try/catch.
6. Smooth motion via requestAnimationFrame and transform/opacity; animation pauses when the tab is hidden where it matters; honours prefers-reduced-motion with a calmer fallback.
7. Pointer events so mouse and touch both work; visible :focus-visible styles; keyboard support where it makes sense.
8. Any sound is synthesized with the Web Audio API, starts only after a user gesture, and has a visible mute/toggle.
9. Premium finish: a deliberate palette and spacing, polished micro-interactions, a beautiful first frame before any interaction, and original copy (no lorem ipsum). Factual content must be accurate; fictional brands, people and data are clearly fictional.
10. Quality bar: visually impressive, bookmark-worthy, showcase-grade, premium, full of delightful details, and clearly distinct from the other 99 pages in concept, layout, palette, typography and motion.


=== DESCRIPTION ===
Helix is a clean, editorial biotech explainer. On the left, a large canvas on an off-white dotted-grid "lab bench" (#f7f9fb) shows an idealised B-DNA double helix, rendered in true 3D with perspective. It is right-handed, has 10.5 base pairs per turn and a 0.34 nm rise, and its two backbones are offset about 135° around the axis, which produces a visibly wide major groove and a narrow minor groove. The helix slowly rotates on a slightly diagonal axis, beside a bold "The Double Helix" headline and a one-turn scale bracket. On the right, a white annotation panel lists five numbered features (5′→3′ direction, sugar–phosphate backbone, major groove, minor groove, hydrogen bonds). Live leader lines run from each note to numbered pins that track the matching feature as the molecule turns. Below the notes are the key measurements, a sequence builder with a colour-coded complementary strand, and a legend. An "Unzip & replicate" sequence animates a simplified semi-conservative replication. A dark mode moves the whole piece to deep navy.

=== MAJOR VISUAL TECHNIQUES ===
- Hand-written 3D pipeline on canvas 2D: model coordinates in ångström, spin about the helix axis, tilt, perspective divide, then an in-plane roll (diagonal on wide screens, near-vertical on phones)
- Correct B-DNA geometry: right-handed twist of 360°/10.5 per bp, 3.4 Å rise, 10 Å radius, 135° backbone offset giving roughly 13 Å and 22 Å grooves; antiparallel strands labelled 5′/3′ at their ends
- Glossy backbone ribbons (#2ec4b6, #e71d36) built from per-segment quads, lit by a Lambert and specular term from the ribbon normal, with phosphate beads and white 5′→3′ chevrons
- Base-pair rungs split at a purine/pyrimidine-weighted point and coloured by nucleotide (A #ff9f1c, T #ffbf69, G #6a4c93, C #8ac926), with specular highlight lines and dashed hydrogen bonds (two for A=T, three for G≡C)
- Depth handled by pooled draw items sorted back to front (painter's algorithm), plus depth fading of back elements toward the page colour (works in both themes)
- Live leader lines: an SVG overlay connects panel anchors to the front-most matching feature each frame (a groove centre, a backbone point, an A–T and a G–C pair); canvas pins carry the numbers
- Replication: a moving fork separates the strands onto two offset axes, free nucleotides fly in along eased wobbling paths, then new lighter-tinted backbones join up into two daughter helices
- Pop-in growth for bases that change when the sequence is edited; a dotted-grid CSS background; a theme-aware palette

=== INTERACTION MODEL ===
- Drag to rotate: movement across the axis spins the helix and movement along it tilts it; spin keeps its inertia and eases back into the auto-rotation. Scroll wheel or pinch to zoom; buttons for pause/play, zoom and reset; keyboard (arrows rotate and tilt, +/− zoom, Space pauses)
- Hover a rung (or tap on touch) to highlight that base pair: a tooltip names both bases, purine or pyrimidine, and the number of hydrogen bonds, and the matching column lights up in the sequence display. Hovering letters in the sequence display highlights the pair in 3D
- Hover an annotation to emphasise its leader line and pin
- Sequence input accepts A/T/G/C only (other characters are stripped with a gentle warning), 2 to 40 bases; the helix rebuilds live with the complementary strand, and GC %, hydrogen-bond count, turns, length and a basic Tm estimate update. A Random button generates a new sequence
- "Unzip & replicate" runs the fork and synthesis with stage captions, then becomes "Rejoin strands" to reverse it
- The dark-mode toggle is saved in localStorage (guarded with try/catch); rendering pauses when the tab is hidden; reduced motion slows rotation and speeds up the replication steps

      <li class="ann" data-k="bb"><span class="pin">2</span><div><h3>Sugar–phosphate backbone</h3><p>Each strand's outer rail: deoxyribose sugars and phosphate groups joined by phosphodiester bonds. The phosphates give DNA its negative charge.</p></div></li>
      <li class="ann" data-k="maj"><span class="pin">3</span><div><h3>Major groove</h3><p>The wide gap, about 2.2 nm across. The edges of the bases are most exposed here, so many DNA-binding proteins read the sequence through it.</p></div></li>
      <li class="ann" data-k="min"><span class="pin">4</span><div><h3>Minor groove</h3><p>The narrow gap, about 1.2 nm across. The grooves differ because the two backbones are not directly opposite each other around the axis.</p></div></li>
      <li class="ann" data-k="hb"><span class="pin">5</span><div><h3>Hydrogen bonds <span class="bond">A=T · 2</span><span class="bond">G≡C · 3</span></h3><p>Adenine pairs with thymine through two hydrogen bonds, and guanine with cytosine through three. A purine always faces a pyrimidine, so every rung is the same width.</p></div></li>
    </ol>

    <h2>Measurements</h2>
    <div class="facts">
      <div class="fact"><b>10.5</b><span>base pairs per turn</span></div>
      <div class="fact"><b>0.34 nm</b><span>rise per base pair</span></div>
      <div class="fact"><b>≈ 3.6 nm</b><span>length of one turn</span></div>
      <div class="fact"><b>≈ 2 nm</b><span>helix diameter</span></div>
    </div>

    <h2>Build a sequence</h2>
    <div class="seqbox">
      <label for="seqIn">Top strand, read 5′ → 3′</label>
      <div class="seqrow">
        <input id="seqIn" type="text" maxlength="40" spellcheck="false" autocomplete="off" autocapitalize="characters" aria-describedby="seqMsg" value="ATGGCTAGCCTAAGTTCGGATCAC">
        <button type="button" class="btn" id="randBtn" aria-label="Random sequence"><svg viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="3" y="3" width="14" height="14" rx="3"/><circle cx="7" cy="7" r=".9" fill="currentColor"/><circle cx="13" cy="13" r=".9" fill="currentColor"/><circle cx="13" cy="7" r=".9" fill="currentColor"/><circle cx="7" cy="13" r=".9" fill="currentColor"/></svg>Random</button>
      </div>
      <p class="msg" id="seqMsg">Type A, T, G or C (2 to 40 bases). The partner strand is generated for you.</p>
      <div class="seq" aria-label="Sequence with its complementary strand">
        <div class="srow"><span class="end">5′</span><span class="bases" id="rowA"></span><span class="end r">3′</span></div>
        <div class="srow"><span class="end"></span><span class="bases hb" id="rowH" aria-hidden="true"></span><span class="end"></span></div>
        <div class="srow"><span class="end">3′</span><span class="bases" id="rowB"></span><span class="end r">5′</span></div>
      </div>
      <div class="stats" id="stats"></div>
      <button type="button" class="btn primary" id="unzipBtn"><svg viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M10 2v5M10 7 5 18M10 7l5 11M7.3 12h5.4"/></svg><span id="unzipLbl">Unzip &amp; replicate</span></button>
    </div>

    <h2>Legend</h2>
    <div class="legend">
      <div class="lg"><i style="background:#ff9f1c"></i><span>Adenine (A)<small>purine · pairs with T</small></span></div>
      <div class="lg"><i style="background:#ffbf69"></i><span>Thymine (T)<small>pyrimidine · pairs with A</small></span></div>
      <div class="lg"><i style="background:#6a4c93"></i><span>Guanine (G)<small>purine · pairs with C</small></span></div>
      <div class="lg"><i style="background:#8ac926"></i><span>Cytosine (C)<small>pyrimidine · pairs with G</small></span></div>
    </div>
    <div class="strands"><span><i style="background:#2ec4b6"></i>Top strand</span><span><i style="background:#e71d36"></i>Partner strand</span><span><i style="background:linear-gradient(90deg,#8ae2d8,#f48c9a)"></i>Newly built strands</span></div>
    <p class="note">The geometry follows idealised B-DNA: 10.5 bp per turn, 0.34 nm rise, about 2 nm across, with the two backbones offset by roughly 135° around the axis. Replication here is simplified: helicase, primase and polymerase are left out, and both new strands are drawn growing in the same direction.</p>
  </aside>
</div>
<svg id="leaders" aria-hidden="true"></svg>

<script>
(() => {
'use strict';
const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
const mq = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)');
let reduced = mq.matches;
if (mq.addEventListener) mq.addEventListener('change', e => { reduced = e.matches; });

/* ---------- theme ---------- */
const root = document.documentElement, themeBtn = $('themeBtn');
const MONO = getComputedStyle(root).getPropertyValue('--mono').trim() || 'monospace';
const SANS = getComputedStyle(root).getPropertyValue('--sans').trim() || 'sans-serif';
let dark = false;
try { dark = localStorage.getItem('helix-theme') === 'dark'; } catch (e) {}
function applyTheme(){
  root.dataset.theme = dark ? 'dark' : 'light';
  themeBtn.setAttribute('aria-pressed', dark ? 'true' : 'false');
  document.querySelector('meta[name="theme-color"]').setAttribute('content', dark ? '#0b1220' : '#f7f9fb');
}
applyTheme();
themeBtn.addEventListener('click', () => { dark = !dark; applyTheme(); try { localStorage.setItem('helix-theme', dark ? 'dark' : 'light'); } catch (e) {} });

/* =====================================================================
   Model constants (Ångström)
   ===================================================================== */
const MAXN = 40, SUB = 4;
const TWIST = 2 * Math.PI / 10.5, RISE = 3.4, RAD = 10, DELTA = 135 * Math.PI / 180, FOCAL = 95, HW = 1.55, RB = 8.4;
const PAIR = { A: 'T', T: 'A', G: 'C', C: 'G' };
const PUR = { A: true, G: true, T: false, C: false };
const NAME = { A: 'Adenine', T: 'Thymine', G: 'Guanine', C: 'Cytosine' };
const BASE = { A: [255, 159, 28], T: [255, 191, 105], G: [106, 76, 147], C: [138, 201, 38] };
const STR = [[46, 196, 182], [231, 29, 54], [244, 140, 154], [138, 226, 216]];

let seq = [], comp = [], n = 0;
const grow = new Float32Array(MAXN).fill(1);
const sep = new Float32Array(MAXN), arrA = new Float32Array(MAXN), arrB = new Float32Array(MAXN);
const spawnA = new Float32Array(MAXN * 3), spawnB = new Float32Array(MAXN * 3), delA = new Float32Array(MAXN), delB = new Float32Array(MAXN);
let mode = 'duplex', mt = 0;

/* =====================================================================
   Canvas + projection
   ===================================================================== */
const viz = $('viz'), cv = $('helix'), ctx = cv.getContext('2d');
let W = 0, H = 0, DPR = 1, landscape = true, cx = 0, cy = 0, k = 10, roll = 0, cR = 1, sR = 0;
const view = { spin: 0.6, spinV: 0, tilt: 0.16, tiltT: 0.16, zoom: 1, zoomT: 1, auto: true };
let cT = 1, sT = 0;
let PX = 0, PY = 0, PD = 0, PS = 1;
function proj(u, v, w){
  const u2 = u * cT - w * sT, w2 = u * sT + w * cT, s = FOCAL / (FOCAL - w2);
  const x = u2 * s * k, y = v * s * k;
  PX = cx + x * cR - y * sR; PY = cy + x * sR + y * cR; PD = w2; PS = s;
}
function layout(){
  const r = viz.getBoundingClientRect();
  DPR = Math.min(2, window.devicePixelRatio || 1); W = Math.max(1, r.width); H = Math.max(1, r.height);
  cv.width = Math.round(W * DPR); cv.height = Math.round(H * DPR);
  ctx.setTransform(DPR, 0, 0, DPR, 0, 0);
  landscape = W > H * 1.05;
  measureAnchors();
}
function frameGeometry(){
  roll = landscape ? -0.24 : -Math.PI / 2 + 0.38; cR = Math.cos(roll); sR = Math.sin(roll);
  cT = Math.cos(view.tilt); sT = Math.sin(view.tilt);
  const L = landscape ? W * 0.8 : Math.min(W / Math.abs(cR), (H - 90) / Math.abs(sR)) * 0.8;
  const risePx = Math.min(landscape ? 46 : W / 14, L / Math.max(n, 8));
  k = risePx / RISE * view.zoom;
  cx = landscape ? W * 0.47 : W / 2; cy = landscape ? H * 0.56 : H * 0.55;
}

/* ---------- colour ---------- */
let BG = [247, 249, 251];
function bgNow(){ return dark ? [11, 18, 32] : [247, 249, 251]; }
function paint(rgb, lit, spec, depth, alpha){
  const fade = Math.pow(Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (RAD - depth) / (2 * RAD))), 1.25) * (dark ? .66 : .6);
  let r = rgb[0] * lit + 255 * spec, g = rgb[1] * lit + 255 * spec, b = rgb[2] * lit + 255 * spec;
  r = Math.min(255, r + (BG[0] - r) * fade); g = Math.min(255, g + (BG[1] - g) * fade); b = Math.min(255, b + (BG[2] - b) * fade);
  return 'rgba(' + (r | 0) + ',' + (g | 0) + ',' + (b | 0) + ',' + alpha.toFixed(3) + ')';
}
const LU = -.28, LV = -.5, LW = .82;
function light(th){
  const nv = Math.cos(th), nw0 = -Math.sin(th);
  const nu = -nw0 * sT, nw = nw0 * cT;
  const d = nu * LU + nv * LV + nw * LW;
  const lit = .42 + .58 * Math.max(0, d) + (nw < 0 ? -.08 : 0);
  const spec = Math.pow(Math.max(0, d), 22) * .65;
  return [lit, spec];
}

/* ---------- item pool (painter's algorithm) ---------- */
const pool = [], list = [];
let pc = 0;
function item(t, d){
  let o = pool[pc];
  if (!o) { o = { t: 0, d: 0, x0: 0, y0: 0, x1: 0, y1: 0, x2: 0, y2: 0, x3: 0, y3: 0, w: 0, c: '', c2: '', n: 0, a: 1, hl: 0 }; pool[pc] = o; }
  pc++; o.t = t; o.d = d; o.hl = 0; o.a = 1; return o;
}

/* strand sample buffers: xL,yL,xR,yR,depth,x,y per sample */
const SB = [0, 1, 2, 3].map(() => new Float32Array(((MAXN - 1) * SUB + 1) * 7));
const easeOut = x => 1 - Math.pow(1 - x, 3);
const smooth = x => x <= 0 ? 0 : x >= 1 ? 1 : x * x * (3 - 2 * x);
const DSEP = RAD * 1.32;
function axisOff(which, s){ return (which === 0 || which === 2 ? 1 : -1) * DSEP * smooth(s); }
function angleOf(which){ return which === 1 || which === 2 ? DELTA : 0; }
function sampleStrand(si){
  const buf = SB[si], m = (n - 1) * SUB + 1;
  for (let s = 0; s < m; s++) {
    const t = s / SUB, i0 = Math.floor(t), i1 = Math.min(n - 1, i0 + 1), f = t - i0;
    const sp = sep[i0] + (sep[i1] - sep[i0]) * f;
    const off = axisOff(si, sp), th = TWIST * t + view.spin + angleOf(si), u = (t - (n - 1) / 2) * RISE;
    const v = RAD * Math.cos(th) + off, w = -RAD * Math.sin(th);
    const o = s * 7;
    proj(u - HW, v, w); buf[o] = PX; buf[o + 1] = PY; const d0 = PD;
    proj(u + HW, v, w); buf[o + 2] = PX; buf[o + 3] = PY;
    proj(u, v, w); buf[o + 4] = (d0 + PD) / 2; buf[o + 5] = PX; buf[o + 6] = PY;
  }
}
function pushRibbon(si, alphaAt){
  const buf = SB[si], m = (n - 1) * SUB + 1, rgb = STR[si];
  for (let s = 0; s < m - 1; s++) {
    const a = alphaAt ? alphaAt(s) : 1;
    if (a <= 0.01) continue;
    const o = s * 7, p = o + 7, t = (s + .5) / SUB, th = TWIST * t + view.spin + angleOf(si);
    const L = light(th), d = (buf[o + 4] + buf[p + 4]) / 2;
    const it = item(0, d);
    it.x0 = buf[o]; it.y0 = buf[o + 1]; it.x1 = buf[o + 2]; it.y1 = buf[o + 3]; it.x2 = buf[p + 2]; it.y2 = buf[p + 3]; it.x3 = buf[p]; it.y3 = buf[p + 1];
    it.c = paint(rgb, L[0], L[1], d, a);
    if (s % SUB === 0 && s > 0 && s < m - SUB) { const bd = item(3, buf[o + 4] + .05); bd.x0 = buf[o + 5]; bd.y0 = buf[o + 6]; bd.w = 1.05 * k * FOCAL / (FOCAL - buf[o + 4]); bd.c = paint([255, 255, 255], .95, 0, buf[o + 4], a * .55); }
  }
}

/* one base half: backbone attachment (angle thX) to the split towards partner (angle thP) around an axis */
const HALF = { x0: 0, y0: 0, x1: 0, y1: 0, d: 0, s: 1, tx: 0, ty: 0, mx: 0, my: 0 };
function baseHalf(i, thX, thP, off, purine, g, du, dv, dw){
  const u = (i - (n - 1) / 2) * RISE + du;
  const xv = RB * Math.cos(thX) + off + dv, xw = -RB * Math.sin(thX) + dw;
  const pv = RB * Math.cos(thP) + off + dv, pw = -RB * Math.sin(thP) + dw;
  const f = (purine ? .545 : .455) - .032;
  const ev = xv + (pv - xv) * f * g, ew = xw + (pw - xw) * f * g;
  proj(u, xv, xw); HALF.x0 = PX; HALF.y0 = PY; const d0 = PD;
  proj(u, ev, ew); HALF.x1 = PX; HALF.y1 = PY; HALF.d = (d0 + PD) / 2; HALF.s = PS;
  const mf = purine ? .545 : .455;
  proj(u, xv + (pv - xv) * mf, xw + (pw - xw) * mf); HALF.mx = PX; HALF.my = PY;
}
function pushHalf(ch, alpha, hl){
  const it = item(1, HALF.d);
  it.x0 = HALF.x0; it.y0 = HALF.y0; it.x1 = HALF.x1; it.y1 = HALF.y1;
  it.w = 1.25 * k * HALF.s;
  it.c = paint(BASE[ch], 1, 0, HALF.d, alpha);
  it.c2 = paint([255, 255, 255], 1, 0, HALF.d, alpha * .38);
  it.hl = hl;
  return it;
}
function pushBonds(x0, y0, x1, y1, count, d, alpha, s){
  const it = item(2, d);
  it.x0 = x0; it.y0 = y0; it.x1 = x1; it.y1 = y1; it.n = count; it.a = alpha; it.w = s;
}

/* hit-testing data, filled every frame */
const hit = new Float32Array(MAXN * 5);
let hover = -1, hoverSeq = -1;

function build(){
  pc = 0;
  const hotHB = annHot === 'hb';
  const inDuplex = mode === 'duplex';
  sampleStrand(0); sampleStrand(1);
  pushRibbon(0, null); pushRibbon(1, null);
  if (!inDuplex) {
    sampleStrand(2); sampleStrand(3);
    const ok = (arr, s) => { const i0 = Math.floor(s / SUB), i1 = Math.min(n - 1, Math.ceil((s + 1) / SUB)); const a = Math.min(arr[i0], arr[i1]); return a < .97 ? 0 : (a - .97) / .03; };
    pushRibbon(2, s => ok(arrA, s)); pushRibbon(3, s => ok(arrB, s));
  }
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const th = TWIST * i + view.spin, a = seq[i], b = comp[i], g = grow[i];
    const sp = sep[i], offA = axisOff(0, sp), offB = axisOff(1, sp);
    const dim = hover >= 0 && hover !== i ? .55 : 1, hl = hover === i ? 1 : 0;
    baseHalf(i, th, th + DELTA, offA, PUR[a], g, 0, 0, 0);
    const hA = pushHalf(a, g * dim, hl); const ax = HALF.x1, ay = HALF.y1, amx = HALF.mx, amy = HALF.my;
    hit[i * 5] = HALF.x0; hit[i * 5 + 1] = HALF.y0;
    baseHalf(i, th + DELTA, th, offB, PUR[b], g, 0, 0, 0);
    const hB = pushHalf(b, g * dim, hl);
    hit[i * 5 + 2] = HALF.x0; hit[i * 5 + 3] = HALF.y0; hit[i * 5 + 4] = (hA.d + hB.d) / 2;
    if (sp < .1) pushBonds(ax, ay, HALF.x1, HALF.y1, a === 'A' || a === 'T' ? 2 : 3, (hA.d + hB.d) / 2 + .01, (1 - sp / .1) * g * dim, HALF.s);
    if (!inDuplex) {
      /* new partner on the top-strand template (sequence = comp) */
      const ea = easeOut(arrA[i]);
      if (arrA[i] > 0) {
        const m = 1 - ea, du = spawnA[i * 3] * m, dv = spawnA[i * 3 + 1] * m + Math.sin(arrA[i] * Math.PI) * 2, dw = spawnA[i * 3 + 2] * m;
        baseHalf(i, th + DELTA, th, offA, PUR[b], 1, du, dv, dw);
        pushHalf(b, Math.min(1, arrA[i] * 2.5), 0);
        const bead = item(3, HALF.d + .02); bead.x0 = HALF.x0; bead.y0 = HALF.y0; bead.w = 1.5 * k * HALF.s; bead.c = paint(STR[2], 1, 0, HALF.d, Math.min(1, arrA[i] * 2.5));
        if (arrA[i] > .9) { baseHalf(i, th, th + DELTA, offA, PUR[a], 1, 0, 0, 0); const tx = HALF.x1, ty = HALF.y1; baseHalf(i, th + DELTA, th, offA, PUR[b], 1, 0, 0, 0); pushBonds(tx, ty, HALF.x1, HALF.y1, a === 'A' || a === 'T' ? 2 : 3, HALF.d + .01, (arrA[i] - .9) * 10, HALF.s); }
      }
      const eb = easeOut(arrB[i]);
      if (arrB[i] > 0) {
        const m = 1 - eb, du = spawnB[i * 3] * m, dv = spawnB[i * 3 + 1] * m - Math.sin(arrB[i] * Math.PI) * 2, dw = spawnB[i * 3 + 2] * m;
        baseHalf(i, th, th + DELTA, offB, PUR[a], 1, du, dv, dw);
        pushHalf(a, Math.min(1, arrB[i] * 2.5), 0);
        const bead = item(3, HALF.d + .02); bead.x0 = HALF.x0; bead.y0 = HALF.y0; bead.w = 1.5 * k * HALF.s; bead.c = paint(STR[3], 1, 0, HALF.d, Math.min(1, arrB[i] * 2.5));
        if (arrB[i] > .9) { baseHalf(i, th + DELTA, th, offB, PUR[b], 1, 0, 0, 0); const tx = HALF.x1, ty = HALF.y1; baseHalf(i, th, th + DELTA, offB, PUR[a], 1, 0, 0, 0); pushBonds(tx, ty, HALF.x1, HALF.y1, a === 'A' || a === 'T' ? 2 : 3, HALF.d + .01, (arrB[i] - .9) * 10, HALF.s); }
      }
    }
  }
  /* direction chevrons on the old strands */
  for (let si = 0; si < 2; si++) {
    const buf = SB[si];
    for (let i = 2; i < n - 1; i += 5) {
      const s = i * SUB, o = s * 7, p = (s + 1) * 7;
      if (buf[o + 4] < RAD * .35) continue;
      let dx = buf[p + 5] - buf[o + 5], dy = buf[p + 6] - buf[o + 6];
      if (si === 1) { dx = -dx; dy = -dy; }
      const it = item(4, buf[o + 4] + .08); it.x0 = buf[o + 5]; it.y0 = buf[o + 6]; it.x1 = Math.atan2(dy, dx); it.w = k * .9 * FOCAL / (FOCAL - buf[o + 4]);
    }
  }
  list.length = pc;
  for (let i = 0; i < pc; i++) list[i] = pool[i];
  list.sort((p, q) => p.d - q.d);
  void hotHB;
}

function draw(){
  BG = bgNow();
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);
  /* axis */
  const u0 = (-(n - 1) / 2 - 1.5) * RISE, u1 = ((n - 1) / 2 + 1.5) * RISE;
  ctx.setLineDash([3, 6]); ctx.lineWidth = 1; ctx.strokeStyle = dark ? 'rgba(231,237,246,.18)' : 'rgba(15,27,45,.16)';
  if (mode === 'duplex') { ctx.beginPath(); proj(u0, 0, 0); ctx.moveTo(PX, PY); proj(u1, 0, 0); ctx.lineTo(PX, PY); ctx.stroke(); }
  ctx.setLineDash([]);
  /* one-turn bracket */
  if (mode === 'duplex' && n >= 12) {
    const a0 = (-(n - 1) / 2) * RISE, a1 = a0 + 10.5 * RISE, vv = RAD + 7;
    ctx.strokeStyle = dark ? 'rgba(231,237,246,.42)' : 'rgba(15,27,45,.38)'; ctx.lineWidth = 1;
    ctx.beginPath(); proj(a0, vv, 0); const bx0 = PX, by0 = PY; ctx.moveTo(PX, PY); proj(a1, vv, 0); ctx.lineTo(PX, PY); const bx1 = PX, by1 = PY; ctx.stroke();
    const nx = -(by1 - by0), ny = bx1 - bx0, nl = Math.hypot(nx, ny) || 1, tx = nx / nl * 5, ty = ny / nl * 5;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(bx0 - tx, by0 - ty); ctx.lineTo(bx0 + tx, by0 + ty); ctx.moveTo(bx1 - tx, by1 - ty); ctx.lineTo(bx1 + tx, by1 + ty); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.save(); ctx.translate((bx0 + bx1) / 2 + tx * 3.2, (by0 + by1) / 2 + ty * 3.2); ctx.rotate(Math.atan2(by1 - by0, bx1 - bx0));
    ctx.fillStyle = dark ? 'rgba(231,237,246,.7)' : 'rgba(15,27,45,.62)'; ctx.font = '600 11px ' + MONO; ctx.textAlign = 'center'; ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
    ctx.fillText('one turn · 10.5 bp · ≈ 3.6 nm', 0, 0); ctx.restore();
  }
  ctx.lineCap = 'round'; ctx.lineJoin = 'round';
  for (let i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
    const it = list[i];
    if (it.t === 0) {
      ctx.fillStyle = it.c; ctx.strokeStyle = it.c; ctx.lineWidth = .8;
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(it.x0, it.y0); ctx.lineTo(it.x1, it.y1); ctx.lineTo(it.x2, it.y2); ctx.lineTo(it.x3, it.y3); ctx.closePath(); ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke();
    } else if (it.t === 1) {
      if (it.hl) { ctx.strokeStyle = dark ? '#ffffff' : '#0f1b2d'; ctx.lineWidth = it.w + 4; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(it.x0, it.y0); ctx.lineTo(it.x1, it.y1); ctx.stroke(); }
      ctx.strokeStyle = it.c; ctx.lineWidth = it.w; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(it.x0, it.y0); ctx.lineTo(it.x1, it.y1); ctx.stroke();
      const dx = it.x1 - it.x0, dy = it.y1 - it.y0, l = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1, ox = -dy / l * it.w * .2, oy = dx / l * it.w * .2;
      ctx.strokeStyle = it.c2; ctx.lineWidth = it.w * .28; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(it.x0 + ox, it.y0 + oy - it.w * .1); ctx.lineTo(it.x1 + ox, it.y1 + oy - it.w * .1); ctx.stroke();
    } else if (it.t === 2) {
      if (it.a <= .01) continue;
      const dx = it.x1 - it.x0, dy = it.y1 - it.y0, l = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1, px = -dy / l, py = dx / l, gap = Math.max(2.2, it.w * k * .34);
      ctx.strokeStyle = dark ? 'rgba(231,237,246,' + (it.a * .9).toFixed(3) + ')' : 'rgba(15,27,45,' + (it.a * .75).toFixed(3) + ')';
      ctx.lineWidth = Math.max(1, k * .12 * it.w); ctx.setLineDash([Math.max(1.5, k * .18), Math.max(1.2, k * .12)]);
      ctx.beginPath();
      for (let b = 0; b < it.n; b++) { const o = (b - (it.n - 1) / 2) * gap; ctx.moveTo(it.x0 + px * o - dx * .12, it.y0 + py * o - dy * .12); ctx.lineTo(it.x1 + px * o + dx * .12, it.y1 + py * o + dy * .12); }
      ctx.stroke(); ctx.setLineDash([]);
    } else if (it.t === 3) {
      ctx.fillStyle = it.c; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(it.x0, it.y0, Math.max(1.2, it.w * .5), 0, 6.2832); ctx.fill();
    } else if (it.t === 4) {
      const s = Math.max(3, it.w * .55);
      ctx.save(); ctx.translate(it.x0, it.y0); ctx.rotate(it.x1);
      ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,.92)'; ctx.lineWidth = Math.max(1.4, s * .32);
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(-s * .5, -s * .6); ctx.lineTo(s * .35, 0); ctx.lineTo(-s * .5, s * .6); ctx.stroke(); ctx.restore();
    }
  }
  /* strand ends */
  if (n > 1) {
    ctx.font = '700 ' + Math.round(Math.max(11, Math.min(15, k * 1.25))) + 'px ' + MONO;
    ctx.textAlign = 'center'; ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
    const ends = [[0, 0, '5′'], [0, n - 1, '3′'], [1, 0, '3′'], [1, n - 1, '5′']];
    for (const [si, i, lab] of ends) {
      const th = TWIST * i + view.spin + angleOf(si), u = (i - (n - 1) / 2) * RISE + (i === 0 ? -4.8 : 4.8);
      proj(u, RAD * Math.cos(th) + axisOff(si, sep[i]), -RAD * Math.sin(th));
      ctx.fillStyle = si === 0 ? '#1aa698' : '#d0162d';
      if (dark) ctx.fillStyle = si === 0 ? '#5ce0d3' : '#ff5a6e';
      ctx.fillText(lab, PX, PY);
    }
  }
  /* pins */
  if (mode === 'duplex' && annAlpha > .02) drawPins();
}

/* =====================================================================
   Annotation targets + leader lines
   ===================================================================== */
const ANN = ['dir', 'bb', 'maj', 'min', 'hb'];
const annEls = [...document.querySelectorAll('.ann')];
let annHot = null, annAlpha = 1;
const targets = {};
function frontMost(lo, hi, fn){
  let best = null, bd = -1e9;
  const a = Math.max(0, Math.floor(n * lo)), b = Math.min(n - 1, Math.ceil(n * hi));
  for (let i = a; i <= b; i++) { const r = fn(i); if (r && r.d > bd) { bd = r.d; best = r; } }
  return best;
}
function surf(i, ang, rad){ const th = TWIST * i + view.spin + ang, u = (i - (n - 1) / 2) * RISE; proj(u, rad * Math.cos(th), -rad * Math.sin(th)); return { x: PX, y: PY, d: PD, i }; }
function computeTargets(){
  if (n < 4) { ANN.forEach(key => { targets[key] = null; }); return; }
  targets.dir = [frontMost(.8, 1, i => surf(i, 0, RAD))];
  targets.bb = [frontMost(.6, .8, i => surf(i, DELTA, RAD))];
  targets.maj = [frontMost(.42, .62, i => surf(i + .5, Math.PI + DELTA / 2, RAD * .96))];
  targets.min = [frontMost(.24, .44, i => surf(i + .5, DELTA / 2, RAD * .92))];
  const pairAt = want => frontMost(.02, .5, i => {
    const at = seq[i] === 'A' || seq[i] === 'T';
    if (want !== at) return null;
    const th = TWIST * i + view.spin, u = (i - (n - 1) / 2) * RISE, f = PUR[seq[i]] ? .545 : .455;
    const xv = RB * Math.cos(th), xw = -RB * Math.sin(th), pv = RB * Math.cos(th + DELTA), pw = -RB * Math.sin(th + DELTA);
    proj(u, xv + (pv - xv) * f, xw + (pw - xw) * f); return { x: PX, y: PY, d: PD, i };
  });
  targets.hb = [pairAt(true), pairAt(false)].filter(Boolean);
}
function drawPins(){
  ctx.font = '700 11px ' + SANS;
  ctx.textAlign = 'center'; ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
  ANN.forEach((key, idx) => {
    const ts = targets[key]; if (!ts) return;
    ts.forEach(t => {
      const hot = annHot === key, r = (hot ? 12 : 9.5) * (landscape ? 1 : .86);
      ctx.globalAlpha = annAlpha;
      ctx.fillStyle = hot ? '#1b6fd8' : (dark ? '#e7edf6' : '#0f1b2d');
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(t.x, t.y, r, 0, 6.2832); ctx.fill();
      ctx.lineWidth = 2; ctx.strokeStyle = dark ? '#0b1220' : '#ffffff'; ctx.stroke();
      ctx.fillStyle = hot ? '#fff' : (dark ? '#0b1220' : '#ffffff');
      ctx.fillText(String(idx + 1), t.x, t.y + .5);
      ctx.globalAlpha = 1;
    });
  });
}
const svgL = $('leaders');
const anchors = [];
function measureAnchors(){
  const panel = document.querySelector('.panel').getBoundingClientRect();
  anchors.length = 0;
  annEls.forEach(el => { const p = el.querySelector('.pin').getBoundingClientRect(); anchors.push({ x: p.left - 4, y: p.top + p.height / 2, edge: panel.left, top: panel.top, bottom: panel.bottom }); });
}
svgL.innerHTML = '<path d=""/>'.repeat(ANN.length * 2);
const leadPaths = ANN.map((key, i) => [svgL.children[i * 2], svgL.children[i * 2 + 1]]);
function updateLeaders(){
  if (getComputedStyle(svgL).display === 'none') return;
  const vr = viz.getBoundingClientRect();
  ANN.forEach((key, i) => {
    const a = anchors[i], ts = targets[key] || [];
    leadPaths[i].forEach((p, j) => {
      const t = ts[j];
      if (!a || !t || mode !== 'duplex' || a.y < a.top + 8 || a.y > a.bottom - 8) { p.setAttribute('d', ''); return; }
      const tx = vr.left + t.x, ty = vr.top + t.y, ex = a.edge - 18 - i * 3;
      const ang = Math.atan2(ty - a.y, tx - ex), r = annHot === key ? 12 : 9.5;
      p.setAttribute('d', 'M' + a.x.toFixed(1) + ' ' + a.y.toFixed(1) + 'H' + ex.toFixed(1) + 'L' + (tx - Math.cos(ang) * r).toFixed(1) + ' ' + (ty - Math.sin(ang) * r).toFixed(1));
      p.style.opacity = annAlpha.toFixed(2);
      p.setAttribute('class', annHot === key ? 'hot' : '');
    });
  });
}
annEls.forEach(el => {
  el.addEventListener('pointerenter', () => { annHot = el.dataset.k; el.classList.add('hot'); });
  el.addEventListener('pointerleave', () => { annHot = null; el.classList.remove('hot'); });
});
document.querySelector('.panel').addEventListener('scroll', measureAnchors, { passive: true });

const seqIn = $('seqIn'), seqMsg = $('seqMsg'), rowA = $('rowA'), rowB = $('rowB'), rowH = $('rowH'), stats = $('stats');
function setSequence(str, animate){
  const old = seq.join('');
  seq = str.split(''); comp = seq.map(c => PAIR[c]);
  const prevN = n; n = seq.length;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) if (animate && (i >= prevN || old[i] !== seq[i])) grow[i] = 0;
  cancelReplication();
  let a = '', b = '', h = '';
  seq.forEach((c, i) => {
    a += '<span class="b-' + c + '" data-i="' + i + '">' + c + '</span>';
    b += '<span class="b-' + comp[i] + '" data-i="' + i + '">' + comp[i] + '</span>';
    h += '<span data-i="' + i + '">' + (c === 'A' || c === 'T' ? '‖' : '⦀') + '</span>';
  });
  rowA.innerHTML = a; rowB.innerHTML = b; rowH.innerHTML = h;
  const gc = seq.filter(c => c === 'G' || c === 'C').length, at = n - gc;
  const tm = n < 14 ? 2 * at + 4 * gc : 64.9 + 41 * (gc - 16.4) / n;
  stats.innerHTML = '<span>Length <b>' + n + ' bp</b> (' + (n * .34).toFixed(1) + ' nm)</span><span>Turns <b>' + (n / 10.5).toFixed(2) + '</b></span><span>GC <b>' + Math.round(gc / n * 100) + '%</b></span><span>H-bonds <b>' + (2 * at + 3 * gc) + '</b></span><span>Tm ≈ <b>' + Math.round(tm) + ' °C</b> <span title="Basic estimate: Wallace rule under 14 bases, otherwise 64.9 + 41(GC − 16.4)/N">(basic estimate)</span></span>';
  frameGeometry(); computeTargets();
}
let msgT = 0;
seqIn.addEventListener('input', () => {
  const raw = seqIn.value, clean = raw.toUpperCase().replace(/[^ATGC]/g, '').slice(0, MAXN);
  if (clean !== raw) {
    const pos = seqIn.selectionStart - (raw.length - clean.length);
    seqIn.value = clean; try { seqIn.setSelectionRange(Math.max(0, pos), Math.max(0, pos)); } catch (e) {}
    if (/[^ATGCatgc]/.test(raw)) { seqMsg.textContent = 'Only A, T, G and C are DNA bases — other letters were left out.'; seqMsg.classList.add('warn'); clearTimeout(msgT); msgT = setTimeout(resetMsg, 2600); }
  }
  if (clean.length >= 2) setSequence(clean, true);
  else { seqMsg.textContent = 'Type at least two bases to build a helix.'; seqMsg.classList.add('warn'); }
});
function resetMsg(){ seqMsg.textContent = 'Type A, T, G or C (2 to 40 bases). The partner strand is generated for you.'; seqMsg.classList.remove('warn'); }
seqIn.addEventListener('blur', () => { if (seqIn.value.length < 2) { seqIn.value = seq.join(''); resetMsg(); } });
$('randBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  const L = 18 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 13); let s = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < L; i++) s += 'ATGC'[Math.floor(Math.random() * 4)];
  seqIn.value = s; resetMsg(); setSequence(s, true);
});
function setSeqHighlight(i){
  if (i === hoverSeq) return;
  [rowA, rowB, rowH].forEach(r => { const o = r.children[hoverSeq]; if (o) o.classList.remove('hl'); const c = r.children[i]; if (c) c.classList.add('hl'); });
  hoverSeq = i;
}
[rowA, rowB, rowH].forEach(r => {
  r.addEventListener('pointerover', e => { const i = e.target.dataset && e.target.dataset.i; if (i !== undefined && mode === 'duplex') { hover = +i; setSeqHighlight(+i); } });
  r.addEventListener('pointerleave', () => { hover = -1; setSeqHighlight(-1); });

   Replication

const unzipBtn = $('unzipBtn'), unzipLbl = $('unzipLbl'), cap = $('cap');
function caption(t){ if (t) { cap.textContent = t; cap.classList.add('on'); } else cap.classList.remove('on'); }
function cancelReplication(){
  mode = 'duplex'; mt = 0; sep.fill(0); arrA.fill(0); arrB.fill(0);
  unzipLbl.textContent = 'Unzip & replicate'; unzipBtn.disabled = false; caption('');
}
function startReplication(){
  if (mode === 'duplex') {
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      spawnA[i * 3] = (Math.random() - .5) * 26; spawnA[i * 3 + 1] = 16 + Math.random() * 20; spawnA[i * 3 + 2] = (Math.random() - .5) * 34;
      spawnB[i * 3] = (Math.random() - .5) * 26; spawnB[i * 3 + 1] = -(16 + Math.random() * 20); spawnB[i * 3 + 2] = (Math.random() - .5) * 34;
      delA[i] = Math.random() * .45; delB[i] = Math.random() * .45;
    }
    mode = 'unzip'; mt = 0; hover = -1; setSeqHighlight(-1); $('tip').classList.remove('on');
    unzipBtn.disabled = true; unzipLbl.textContent = 'Replicating…';
    caption('Hydrogen bonds break and the strands separate');
  } else if (mode === 'done') {
    mode = 'rejoin'; mt = 0; unzipBtn.disabled = true; unzipLbl.textContent = 'Rejoining…';
    caption('Returning to the original double helix');
  }
}
unzipBtn.addEventListener('click', startReplication);
function stepReplication(dt){
  if (mode === 'duplex') return;
  const sp = reduced ? 2.2 : 1;
  mt += dt * sp;
  if (mode === 'unzip' || mode === 'synth' || mode === 'done') {
    const T1 = 2.6, fork = mt / T1 * 1.25;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      sep[i] = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (fork - i / n) * 3.2));
      const start = .55 + (i / n) * T1 * .95;
      arrA[i] = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (mt - start - delA[i]) / .95));
      arrB[i] = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (mt - start - delB[i]) / .95));
    }
    if (mode === 'unzip' && mt > 1.1) { mode = 'synth'; caption('Free nucleotides pair with each exposed base: A with T, G with C'); }
    if (mode === 'synth' && mt > .55 + T1 * .95 + .45 + .95 + .2) {
      mode = 'done'; unzipBtn.disabled = false; unzipLbl.textContent = 'Rejoin strands';
      caption('Two daughter helices, each keeping one original strand: semi-conservative replication');
    }
  } else if (mode === 'rejoin') {
    const k1 = Math.min(1, mt / 1.1);
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { arrA[i] = Math.min(arrA[i], 1 - k1); arrB[i] = Math.min(arrB[i], 1 - k1); }
    if (mt > 1.1) {
      const f = (mt - 1.1) / 1.6 * 1.25;
      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) sep[i] = Math.min(sep[i], Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (1.25 - f - (1 - i / n)) * 3.2)));
    }
    if (mt > 2.9) { cancelReplication(); }
  }
}

const tip = $('tip');
const pts = new Map();
let dragging = false, lastX = 0, lastY = 0, velPerp = 0, pinch0 = 0, zoom0 = 1, idleAt = 0;
cv.addEventListener('pointerdown', e => {
  pts.set(e.pointerId, [e.clientX, e.clientY]);
  try { cv.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId); } catch (err) {}
  if (pts.size === 1) { dragging = true; lastX = e.clientX; lastY = e.clientY; velPerp = 0; cv.classList.add('dragging'); }
  if (pts.size === 2) { const [a, b] = [...pts.values()]; pinch0 = Math.hypot(a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1]); zoom0 = view.zoomT; }
});
cv.addEventListener('pointermove', e => {
  if (pts.has(e.pointerId)) pts.set(e.pointerId, [e.clientX, e.clientY]);
  if (pts.size === 2) { const [a, b] = [...pts.values()]; const d = Math.hypot(a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1]); if (pinch0 > 0) view.zoomT = Math.max(.55, Math.min(2.8, zoom0 * d / pinch0)); return; }
  const r = cv.getBoundingClientRect(), mx = e.clientX - r.left, my = e.clientY - r.top;
  if (dragging) {
    const dx = e.clientX - lastX, dy = e.clientY - lastY; lastX = e.clientX; lastY = e.clientY;
    const perp = landscape ? dy * cR - dx * sR : dx, along = landscape ? dx * cR + dy * sR : -dy;
    view.spin += perp * .011; velPerp = perp * .011 * 60;
    view.tiltT = Math.max(-1.05, Math.min(1.05, view.tiltT + along * .005));
    idleAt = performance.now();
    return;
  }
  if (e.pointerType === 'mouse') pick(mx, my, e.clientX, e.clientY);
});
const endPtr = e => {
  pts.delete(e.pointerId);
  if (pts.size < 2) pinch0 = 0;
  if (pts.size === 0) { dragging = false; cv.classList.remove('dragging'); view.spinV = velPerp; }
  if (e.pointerType !== 'mouse' && e.type === 'pointerup') { const r = cv.getBoundingClientRect(); pick(e.clientX - r.left, e.clientY - r.top, e.clientX, e.clientY); }
};
cv.addEventListener('pointerup', endPtr);
cv.addEventListener('pointercancel', endPtr);
cv.addEventListener('pointerleave', e => { if (e.pointerType === 'mouse' && !dragging) { hover = -1; setSeqHighlight(-1); tip.classList.remove('on'); } });
cv.addEventListener('wheel', e => {
  e.preventDefault();
  const d = Math.max(-110, Math.min(110, e.deltaMode === 1 ? e.deltaY * 33 : e.deltaY));
  view.zoomT = Math.max(.55, Math.min(2.8, view.zoomT * Math.exp(-d * .0013)));
}, { passive: false });
function pick(mx, my, clientX, clientY){
  if (mode !== 'duplex') { hover = -1; tip.classList.remove('on'); return; }
  let best = -1, bd = 1e9;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const x0 = hit[i * 5], y0 = hit[i * 5 + 1], x1 = hit[i * 5 + 2], y1 = hit[i * 5 + 3];
    const dx = x1 - x0, dy = y1 - y0, L = dx * dx + dy * dy || 1;
    const t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, ((mx - x0) * dx + (my - y0) * dy) / L));
    const d = Math.hypot(mx - (x0 + dx * t), my - (y0 + dy * t)) - hit[i * 5 + 4] * .25;
    if (d < bd) { bd = d; best = i; }
  }
  const lim = Math.max(10, k * 1.1);
  if (best >= 0 && bd < lim) {
    hover = best; setSeqHighlight(best);
    const a = seq[best], b = comp[best], at = a === 'A' || a === 'T';
    tip.innerHTML = '<b>' + a + (at ? '=' : '≡') + b + '</b> <i>· pair ' + (best + 1) + ' of ' + n + '</i><br>' + NAME[a] + ' (' + (PUR[a] ? 'purine' : 'pyrimidine') + ') with ' + NAME[b] + ' (' + (PUR[b] ? 'purine' : 'pyrimidine') + ')<br>' + (at ? 2 : 3) + ' hydrogen bonds';
    const vr = viz.getBoundingClientRect();
    let tx = clientX - vr.left, ty = clientY - vr.top;
    if (tx > vr.width - 270) tx -= 280;
    if (ty > vr.height - 110) ty -= 110;
    tip.style.left = tx + 'px'; tip.style.top = ty + 'px'; tip.classList.add('on');
  } else { hover = -1; setSeqHighlight(-1); tip.classList.remove('on'); }
}
cv.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
  const key = e.key; let used = true;
  if (key === 'ArrowLeft') view.spin -= .18; else if (key === 'ArrowRight') view.spin += .18;
  else if (key === 'ArrowUp') view.tiltT = Math.max(-1.05, view.tiltT - .12); else if (key === 'ArrowDown') view.tiltT = Math.min(1.05, view.tiltT + .12);
  else if (key === '+' || key === '=') view.zoomT = Math.min(2.8, view.zoomT * 1.2); else if (key === '-' || key === '_') view.zoomT = Math.max(.55, view.zoomT / 1.2);
  else if (key === ' ') toggleAuto(); else used = false;
  if (used) { e.preventDefault(); idleAt = performance.now(); }
});

$('zoomOut').addEventListener('click', () => { view.zoomT = Math.max(.55, view.zoomT / 1.25); });
$('resetBtn').addEventListener('click', () => { view.zoomT = 1; view.tiltT = .16; view.spinV = 0; });

/* =====================================================================
   Loop
   ===================================================================== */
let last = 0, raf = 0, leaderTick = 0;
function frame(now){
  const dt = last ? Math.min(.05, (now - last) / 1000) : .016; last = now;
  const autoSpeed = view.auto ? (reduced ? .12 : .42) : 0;
  if (!dragging) {
    view.spinV += (autoSpeed - view.spinV) * Math.min(1, dt * 1.6);
    view.spin += view.spinV * dt;
  }
  view.tilt += (view.tiltT - view.tilt) * Math.min(1, dt * 6);
  view.zoom += (view.zoomT - view.zoom) * Math.min(1, dt * 7);
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) if (grow[i] < 1) grow[i] = Math.min(1, grow[i] + dt * (reduced ? 6 : 2.4));
  stepReplication(dt);
  annAlpha += ((mode === 'duplex' ? 1 : 0) - annAlpha) * Math.min(1, dt * 6);
  frameGeometry();
  build();
  computeTargets();
  draw();
  leaderTick += dt;
  if (leaderTick > .5) { leaderTick = 0; measureAnchors(); }
  updateLeaders();
  raf = requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}
function start(){ if (!raf) { last = 0; raf = requestAnimationFrame(frame); } }
function stop(){ if (raf) cancelAnimationFrame(raf); raf = 0; }
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => { document.hidden ? stop() : start(); });
let rt = 0;
window.addEventListener('resize', () => { clearTimeout(rt); rt = setTimeout(layout, 60); });

layout();
setSequence(seqIn.value.toUpperCase().replace(/[^ATGC]/g, '') || 'ATGGCTAGCCTAAGTTCGGATCAC', false);
start();
})();

FILE: apps/dna/app.nim
